old: A 1993 10-cent coin from Jamaica. One side shows the coat of arms of Jamaica. A crocodile sits on top. Two Taino people hold the shield. The shield has a cross with pineapples on it. The coin also says JAMAICA, TEN CENTS, and 1993. It also says the motto OUT OF MANY, ONE PEOPLE. The coin is made of steel with a thin coat of nickel on it.

old: A 1967 20-centavo coin from Mexico. The front shows the coat of arms of Mexico. The back shows the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan. Two volcanoes stand behind it. Their names are Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl. A liberty cap shines above the pyramid. The back also has a big 20, the word CENTAVOS, the date 1967, and the Mo mint mark. The coin is made of brass. The brass is 95% copper and 5% zinc.
